verses.1:1: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of the elect of God and the knowledge of the truth which is according to godliness,
verses.1:2: in hope of eternal life, which God, who does not lie, promised before the times of the ages;
verses.1:3: but at His own times He manifested His word in the preaching which was entrusted to me according to the command of God our Savior.
verses.1:4: To Titus, a beloved son according to the common faith: grace and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Savior.
verses.1:5: For this reason I left you in Crete, so that you may set right the things that are lacking and appoint elders throughout the cities, just as I also directed you:
verses.1:6: if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children, not under accusation of debauchery nor insubordinate.
verses.1:7: For an overseer must be blameless, as God's steward: not arrogant, not hot-tempered, not addicted to wine, not violent, not greedy for shameful gain,
verses.1:8: but hospitable, kind, sober, righteous, holy, self-controlled,
verses.1:9: embracing the faithful word which is according to the teaching, so that he may be able to exhort in sound teaching and to reprove those who contradict.
verses.1:10: For there are also many who are disobedient, empty talkers, and deceivers, especially those who are of the circumcision,
verses.1:11: who must be refuted, who subvert entire households, teaching what they should not for the sake of shameful gain.
verses.1:12: One of them, a prophet of their own, said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies."
verses.1:13: This testimony is true. Because of this, rebuke them severely, so that they may be sound in the faith,
verses.1:14: not paying attention to Jewish fables and commands of people who turn themselves away from the truth.
verses.1:15: All things are clean to those who are clean, but to the defiled and unbelieving nothing is clean; rather, both their mind and conscience are defiled.
verses.1:16: They profess that they know God, but by their deeds they deny Him, since they are detestable, unbelieving, and disqualified for every good work.
verses.2:1: But as for you, speak the things that are fitting for sound teaching:
verses.2:2: that older men be sober, modest, prudent, sound in faith, in love, in patience;
verses.2:3: that older women likewise be in holy demeanor, not slanderers, not enslaved to much wine, teaching well,
verses.2:4: so that they may teach prudence to the younger women, to love their husbands, to love their children,
verses.2:5: to be prudent, chaste, sober, taking care of the home, kind, subject to their own husbands, so that the word of God may not be blasphemed.
verses.2:6: Likewise, exhort the younger men to be sober.
verses.2:7: In all things present yourself as an example of good works, in teaching, in integrity, in dignity,
verses.2:8: sound, irreproachable speech, so that the one who is on the opposing side may be ashamed, having nothing evil to say about us.
verses.2:9: Servants are to be subject to their own masters, pleasing in all things, not contradicting,
verses.2:10: not defrauding, but showing good faith in all things, so that they may adorn the teaching of God our Savior in all things.
verses.2:11: For the grace of God our Savior has appeared to all people,
verses.2:12: training us so that, renouncing ungodliness and worldly desires, we may live soberly, righteously, and in a godly manner in this age,
verses.2:13: awaiting the blessed hope and the coming of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ,
verses.2:14: who gave Himself for us, so that He might redeem us from all iniquity and cleanse for Himself an acceptable people, a pursuer of good works.
verses.2:15: Speak these things, and exhort, and reprove with all authority. Let no one despise you.
verses.3:1: Remind them to be subject to rulers and authorities, to obey commands, to be ready for every good work,
verses.3:2: to slander no one, not to be quarrelsome, but gentle, showing all meekness toward all people.
verses.3:3: For we also were once foolish, unbelieving, going astray, enslaved to desires and various pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, hating one another.
verses.3:4: But when the kindness and benevolence of God our Savior appeared,
verses.3:5: not from works of righteousness which we ourselves did, but according to His mercy He saved us, through the washing of regeneration and renewal of the Holy Spirit,
verses.3:6: whom He poured out upon us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,
verses.3:7: so that, justified by His grace, we may be heirs according to the hope of eternal life.
verses.3:8: The word is faithful, and I want you to insist on these things, so that those who believe in God may take care to excel in good works. These things are good and useful for people.
verses.3:9: But avoid foolish questions, and genealogies, and disputes, and quarrels about the law; for they are useless and futile.
verses.3:10: Avoid a heretical person after a first and second correction,
verses.3:11: knowing that such a person is subverted and sins, being condemned by his own judgment.
verses.3:12: When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, hurry to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have decided to spend the winter there.
verses.3:13: Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their way with care, so that nothing may be lacking to them.
verses.3:14: And let our people also learn to excel in good works for necessary uses, so that they may not be unfruitful.
verses.3:15: All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in the faith. The grace of God be with all of you. Amen.

notes.1:2: Latin ante tempora saecularia, literally "before the times of the ages," renders the Greek expression for "before eternal times."
notes.1:4: The Vulgate reads dilecto filio ("beloved son"), whereas the Greek reads "true/genuine child."
notes.1:11: The Vulgate uses redargui ("be refuted" or "reproved"), where the Greek uses a verb meaning "to silence" or "muzzle."
notes.1:16: In Christian Latin of the Vulgate, incredibiles is used actively for "unbelieving" or "refusing obedience," rendering the Greek term for "disobedient."
notes.2:5: The Clementine Vulgate lists six qualities here, adding sobrias ("sober") alongside prudentes ("prudent"), whereas the Greek lists five.
notes.2:8: The Vulgate reads de nobis ("about us"), where many Greek manuscripts read "about you."
notes.2:11: The Vulgate reads gratia Dei Salvatoris nostri ("the grace of God our Savior"), rendering the Greek adjective for "bringing salvation" as the genitive title "of our Savior."
notes.2:13: The Vulgate uses adventum ("coming") for Greek "appearing"; the Latin genitive magni Dei, et Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi can refer either to Jesus Christ alone as "the great God and our Savior" or to God the Father and Jesus Christ.
notes.2:14: The Vulgate renders Greek "a people for His own possession" with populum acceptabilem ("an acceptable people").
notes.3:5: Both genitives, regenerationis and renovationis, depend on lavacrum ("washing"), the accusative object of per: "the washing of regeneration and of renewal of the Holy Spirit."
notes.3:8: Latin bonis operibus praeesse (also in 3:14) literally means "to stand at the head of" or "lead in good works," rendering a Greek verb meaning "to devote oneself to" or "take the lead in."
notes.3:10: The Vulgate renders the Greek term for "factious" or "divisive" with the Christian Latin word haereticum ("heretical").
notes.3:15: The Clementine Vulgate includes Dei ("of God") in "The grace of God" and concludes with "Amen," whereas most critical Greek texts read simply "Grace be with all of you."
